_about: R17 rodeo arena and saloon (plan_rodeo.js): every name and line of copy, the schedule, the riders, the staff talk cards, the roaming people and the stamp proposal. Edit the copy here; the module has the same values built in as a fallback.

venue.p: An Old West saloon and steakhouse joined to a working rodeo arena in the North Yard. Douglas grew up as a copper smelter town, so the name had to have copper in it. Bull riding and saddle bronc every evening, slack in the afternoon, brisket on the terrace.

arena.k: The Copper Chute · deep dirt, pipe fence
arena.p: Forty-eight metres of deep raked dirt inside a pipe fence, four bucking chutes on the saloon side, a return alley to the pens and six light towers for night events. The grandstand is covered; the regulars watch from the saloon deck.

chutes.k: Four chutes · the catwalk · the lead-up alley
chutes.p: Bulls and broncs come up the alley from the pens into the chutes. Riders settle on from the catwalk, wrap the rope and nod. The gate swings toward the arena and the clock starts.

stand.k: Seven rows under a corrugated roof
stand.p: Covered seating along the arena, slatted end screens against the low afternoon sun from the south-west. Press E by a seat to sit and watch the next ride.

pens.k: Bulls, broncs and the pickup horses
pens.p: Four pens on the slope behind the chutes, with water and hay. The return alley brings the stock back after every ride.

remuda.p: A string of trail horses and pickup horses from the Frontier Ranch, brought up for rodeo nights. Abel the wrangler looks after them.

smoker.p: An offset smoker on its trailer: mesquite and oak, brisket and ribs, low and slow. Big Lou runs it. Picnic tables under the ramada and string lights after dark.

deck.k: The rail bar over the arena
deck.p: A covered deck along the arena with a rail bar and stools, wrapping round to the BBQ terrace. When the chutes open, this is where the regulars sit.

stage.p: A band stage under a painted mural of the arena at sunset. Two-step on the dance floor; the jukebox by the door fills in between sets.

bar.p: A bar front burned with ranch brands, a brass rail and the back bar under the longhorn. Della runs it: sarsaparilla, coffee and a steak plate from the kitchen.

lot.p: Park the cart here on rodeo nights and walk across Night Field Road to the saloon porch.

booth.p: The stand over the chutes, with the scoreboard on its roof. Every ride is called from up here.

talk.t: Welcome to the Copper Chute. Saloon up front, steakhouse in back, and the best seat in the house is the rail on the deck when the chutes open. What can I get you?
Douglas grew up around the copper smelters, so a place in this town had to have copper in its name. The chute is where every ride starts: eight seconds that feel like an hour.

Slack runs in the afternoon, two to four, when the young riders practice. Rodeo Night starts at half past six every evening: bulls and broncs under the lights, Hollis on the microphone. The iron bull in here runs all day.
Brisket has been on since four this morning. Mesquite and oak, low and slow, a little salt and a lot of patience. Grab a plate and a seat under the ramada.
No secret. Keep the fire small, keep the lid shut, and never trust anybody who is in a hurry with a brisket.

greet: Stay outside the fence when the gates open.

talk.t: I run the arena. Four chutes, two pens of bulls, broncs in the back pens and two bullfighters who earn every dollar. Watch from the grandstand or the saloon deck, and stay outside the fence when the gates open.
o: Can I go behind the chutes?

talk.t: The rider nods, the gate swings, and they have to stay on for eight seconds with one hand. The judges score the rider and the animal. Touch the animal with the free hand and it is a no score.
Up on the catwalk, sure. Keep your hands out of the chutes and give the riders room when they climb down.
That is the iron bull. Step into the ring and press E. Lean with it when it turns, A or D, and hit SPACE when it bucks. Eight seconds and you go on the board.
Watch its shoulders, not your hands. It always tells you where it is going.
These are trail horses from the Frontier Ranch. We bring a string up for rodeo nights: the pickup horses, and a few for anyone who wants to see a good horse up close.
The bay with the blue blanket. Fourteen years old and still the first one to the gate.
Hollis Grant, the voice of the Copper Chute. From up here I can see every chute and every seat. Best show in the North Yard, and I am not just saying that because I work here.

{rider} nods for {animal} in chute {n}. Here we go!
score: That is the whistle! {score} points for {rider}!
thrown: {animal} wins that round. Give {rider} a hand, folks, that is all we get.
Down goes {rider}! The bullfighters earn their pay tonight.
{animal} sends {rider} into the dirt. No time!

prompts.juke: A two-step comes on. The floor fills up.
prompts.ride: Hold on! Lean with A and D (or the arrows) when it turns, SPACE when it bucks.
prompts.won: EIGHT SECONDS! You rode the iron bull. Best {best} s
prompts.thrown: Thrown at {t} s. Best {best} s. Junie says: lean into the turn.
